title: Resolve outboxProcessor lazily in syncOrchestratorProvider instead of capturing it by value
rule: SM-6 lazy-resolver consistency / Nygard-lens: stale capture across DB swap
why: Every other volatile build-time dependency in this same constructor call (gateway, merge router, outbox DAO, identity status) is deliberately passed as a lazy `() => ref.read(...)` resolver specifically — per the inline comments at lines 136-137, 161-163 — 'so a DB swap (multi-account flow) is picked up without rebuilding the orchestrator singleton.' outboxProcessor is the one exception: it's read once (line 129) and stored as a plain value field. outboxProcessorProvider (outbox_providers.dart) watches userDatabaseProvider and rebuilds on a DB swap; database_provider.dart confirms userDatabaseProvider swaps via the independently-mutable accountDbFileNameProvider, decoupled from authStateProvider (the only thing syncOrchestratorProvider itself watches). If a DB swap can occur without authStateProvider's watched value also changing in the same tick, the orchestrator keeps draining through an OutboxProcessor bound to the pre-swap, superseded UserDatabase/outboxDao while its other lazily-resolved collaborators (gateway, merge router) may already be pointing at the new account — a split-identity state. Confirming this needs tracing whether the app's account-switch flow (account_actions.dart) can complete a DB swap before authStateProvider's emitted value settles to the new account.
recommendation: Change the outboxProcessor parameter to a lazy `resolveOutboxProcessor: () => ref.read(outboxProcessorProvider)` resolver, matching resolveGateway/resolveMergeRouter/resolveOutboxDao, so it can't go stale relative to its siblings.
acceptance_criteria: syncOrchestratorProvider resolves outboxProcessor via a lazy resolver rather than a captured value.

Regression/integration test: trigger a userDatabaseProvider swap while syncOrchestratorProvider stays alive (authState unchanged) and assert the next drain operates against the new outboxDao's pending rows, not the pre-swap instance.

corrections: 'gateway... may already be pointing at the new account' is wrong: firestoreGatewayProvider depends on authStateProvider, not userDatabaseProvider, so it stays old in lockstep with outboxProcessor during the window. The actually-divergent siblings are resolveMergeRouter (comment confirms it watches userDatabaseProvider) and resolveOutboxDao (directly reads userDatabaseProvider) — same race, wrong example cited in the 'why'.
